title: cross-tenant-session-reuse-after-api-key-rotation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Several customers across Hosted and Dedicated reported that API requests authenticated with an API key recently rotated by their org were still accepted for up to 2 minutes after rotation, and in some cases requests were attributed to the wrong org. This ticket tracks triage, hotfixes, and long-term mitigations for the token/credential refresh and cache-coherence issues impacting API key revocation and org scoping.
impact_summary: Multiple mid-market customers observed brief windows where revoked API keys remained valid or were mapped to the wrong tenant. Impact included exposure of responses to the wrong org in edge cases, incorrect billing attribution, and significant customer escalations for Hosted and Dedicated customers. Private deployments using our proxy cache also reported similar symptoms when KMS-backed key metadata lagged.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create API key for org A and perform requests to /v1/generate to warm caches
2) Rotate API key via admin API (POST /orgs/:id/keys/rotate) which issues new key and marks old key revoked
3) Immediately send requests using the old key from parallel clients (concurrent TTL refresh) and from a client using a header tenant override used in some SDKs
4) Observe accepted responses for the old key for ~30-120s and in two cases responses contain org B's resource identifiers when node affinity rebalanced.
observed_behavior: Revoked API keys accepted briefly; request handling path sometimes resolved tenant context incorrectly during a concurrent refresh and node migration. Logs show that API gateway accepted token, forwarded to runtime, which used a stale in-memory key->org cache on GPU inference node leading to mismatched tenant attribution.
expected_behavior: API key revocation should take effect within seconds and always preserve correct tenant mapping. No revoked key should be served after rotation, and tenant context must be strictly derived from authoritative control plane state.
root_cause: Race between control-plane key state propagation and per-node in-memory cache invalidation. Two contributing factors: (1) The refresh flow increments a per-org token-generation counter but the dedicated runtime nodes constructed a short-lived cache key that included only the API key fingerprint and node affinity tag, enabling a stale mapping when node affinity changed. (2) A background KMS metadata refresh had a 2-minute default TTL in Private installs, allowing revoked keys to remain accepted until next metadata sweep.
immediate_mitigation: 1) Deploy hotfix to hosted control plane to publish key-revocation events via pub/sub with immediate node invalidation path (hotfix CHERRY-PICK PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8452)
2) Emergency rollback of the last affinity-affecting scheduler change in dedicated pools to avoid mid-request node migration (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/477)

3) For Private customers, push advisory and patch to reduce KMS metadata TTL to 5s and provide manual invalidation script (confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SEC/pages/Key+Revocation+Runbook)
4) Add a temporary gating rule at API gateway to reject requests with keys revoked within last 5 minutes if node-level statement mismatch detected (WAF rule id: WAF-2987)
5) Notified affected customers, opened support tickets, and enabled request-level auditing for suspicious tenant-attribution events.
long_term_fix: Revamp key->tenant caching: move to versioned mapping keyed by (api_key_fingerprint, revision_id) propagated with causal ordering. Implement immediate invalidation API and leverage the control plane pub/sub to update runtime nodes atomically. Add end-to-end tests that simulate concurrent rotations, node migration, and KMS metadata TTL variance. Update Private installer to default safe TTLs and expose an operator API for manual invalidation.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (hotfix): hosted rollout to us-east-1 then global in 30min windows, dedicated pools first run in canary group (1 pool), private customers receive patch with manual instructions
Phase 2: deploy cache-versioning change to runtime in canary and run 48-hour soak with synthetic rotations at scale
Phase 3: coordinated upgrade of orchestrator affinity scheduler and remove temporary gating rules after verification
Phase 4: postmortem and docs update; deprecate old metadata TTL defaults in private installer
notes: PM and SRE paged on 2026-03-10 03:42 UTC; customers with Dedicated plans escalated to SEs.
Investigation showed correlated spikes in scheduler rebalancing and KMS metadata refresh windows.
We must add synthetic chaos tests for key rotation as part of CI for runtime and orchestrator.
